plot: On a sunny morning Max and Grandma try to pull a giant carrot out of the garden; Dog joins the tug, Bird's flapping tickles Dog so everyone tumbles, and the carrot only pops out when tiny Mouse adds her pull at the end of the line, and Grandma bakes a carrot cake where the smallest helper gets the first crumb.

beats.say: Heave... ho... heave... whoa!
It is a sunny morning in Grandma's vegetable garden. And something very big is growing.
Max, dear, are you all right? You flew like a pancake!
Grandma, your carrot is stuck! I pulled and pulled, and I fell on my bottom.
That carrot? I planted it in the spring. It grew and grew all summer long.
Look at those leaves. They are almost as tall as you!
Then it must be the biggest carrot in the whole world. Let's pull together!
Grandma holds the leaves. Max holds Grandma. One, two, three, pull!
The leaves wiggle. The ground wiggles. But the carrot does not come out.
My, my. It is holding on very tight. We need more help.
Dog! Dog! Can you come and pull with us?
Pull? Like tug of war? I am the tug of war champion!
Dog holds Max. Max holds Grandma. Grandma holds the leaves. Pull!
Grrr! Come out, carrot! I am very, very strong!
They pull so hard that Dog's ears flap like flags. But the carrot stays in the ground.
That carrot is stronger than me. I think I need a snack.
Dog, you can't stop now. Snacks come after the pulling!
Hello! What is this? A long line of friends? Is it a dance?
Bird lands on top of the carrot leaves, and looks down at everybody.
It is a carrot pull! Bird, will you help us?
I am small, but my wings are mighty! Flap, flap, flap!
Bird holds Dog's tail. Everyone pulls. Bird flaps so hard that feathers fly.
Ha ha ha! Bird, your flapping is tickling my tail!
Dog giggles and lets go. And everybody tumbles into one big, silly pile.
Oh no. Grandma, maybe this carrot wants to stay in the ground forever.
Don't give up yet, Max. Is there anyone we have not asked?
Everyone thinks. Then a tiny voice comes from behind a flower.
Excuse me. Can I help too? I am very small, but I am good at holding.
You? But you are tinier than one carrot leaf!
Tiny paws can hold on very tight. Just watch me!
Every helper counts, Dog. Come on, Mouse. Hold on to Bird!
Mouse holds Bird. Bird holds Dog. Dog holds Max. Max holds Grandma. Grandma holds the leaves.
Ready, everyone? One... two... three... pull!
They pull, and pull, and pull. And then...
Out comes the carrot! It is huge, and orange, and even bigger than Max!
Wow! It is as big as a tree! Well, a small tree. A baby tree.
Can I eat it? Can I eat it right now?
We did it! And I helped, even though I am tiny!
Yes, Mouse. Your little pull was the one that made it pop.
So it was not the strongest friend. It was all the friends, together.
And a mouse! Don't forget the mouse!
Now, what shall we do with such a big carrot?
Soup? Salad? A carrot boat? A carrot hat?
I think I will bake a big carrot cake. Enough for everyone.
Later that day, Grandma brings out a warm orange cake, with one little candle on top.
It smells like sunshine and carrots!
I am not even sad about the snack anymore. This is the best snack!
Can I have the first crumb? Just a tiny one?
The smallest helper gets the first piece. That is the rule today.
So everybody shares the carrot cake, under the big blue sky.
Tomorrow we plant a pumpkin seed. I hope it grows as big as a house!
